parts.title: Hiring a car
parts.context: A man phones a car hire company to book a car for a family holiday.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Part 1. You will hear a man phoning a car hire company. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: You will see that there is an example that has been done for you. On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Good afternoon, Coastline Car Hire, Sophie speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: Hello. I'd like to hire a car for a family holiday next month. We're flying in, so could we pick it up at the airport?

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Of course. We have a desk at the airport.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: The man wants to collect the car at the airport, so 'airport' has been written in the space. Now we shall begin. You should answer the questions as you listen, because you will not hear the recording a second time. Listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Can I have your surname, please?

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: It's Fenwick. F-E-N-W-I-C-K.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Thank you, Mr Fenwick. And how long will you need the car?

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: We arrive on the third of August, and we fly home a week later, so seven days.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Seven days. What kind of car were you thinking of?

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: I was going to book something small to keep the cost down, but we're bringing our bikes, so I think we'd better have an estate car. They've got more room at the back.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: An estate. Will you need any extras?

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: Yes, a child seat, please. Our daughter's four.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: No problem. And will anyone else be driving?

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: My wife will drive as well, so please add her to the booking.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: How much will it cost?

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: An estate is normally forty-five pounds a day, but because you're booking a whole week, it comes down to thirty-eight pounds a day.

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: That's good. What about insurance?

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Basic insurance is included, but if there's any damage you pay the first thousand pounds. Most families choose full cover, which means you pay nothing at all.

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: With two children in the back, I think we'd better have the full cover.

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Very sensible. The car will have a full tank when you collect it, and you need to bring it back with a full tank too, or there's a refuelling charge.

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: OK. Where exactly is your desk?

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: It's in the arrivals hall, opposite the coffee shop. You can't miss it.

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: And what do I need to bring?

script.speaker: sophie
script.text: Your driving licence, of course, and your passport. We can't give you the car without both.

script.speaker: fenwick
script.text: Great. Thanks for your help.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

parts.title: Summer jobs at an adventure park
parts.context: The manager of an adventure park welcomes new summer staff.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Part 2. You will hear the manager of an adventure park talking to new summer staff. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Treetop Adventure Park. I'm Rachel, the operations manager. I know it's your first day, so I'll keep this short.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: We want you to be friendly with our visitors, and of course we expect you to be on time for every shift. But nothing, absolutely nothing, matters more than the safety checks. Every harness and every rope must be checked before each group starts, even if you checked it ten minutes earlier.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: You'll each receive two T-shirts and a jacket. The uniform is free, and you can keep it at the end of the summer. But please don't wear your own jackets over it, because visitors need to be able to see who works here.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: You'll be paid every two weeks, on a Friday, straight into your bank account. Your first payment will be on the twentieth of June.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: And the weather. We don't close for rain. Visitors come prepared. But if there's thunder or lightning, the high ropes course closes immediately, and the staff from that area will help out in the rest of the park until the storm has passed.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: Now, where you'll be working for the first two weeks. Amir, you've worked with children before, so you'll be in the children's play zone.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: Bella, I know you asked for the climbing wall, but you need the instructor's certificate first, and the next course isn't until July. So for now, you'll be in the ticket office.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: Chris already has his climbing instructor qualification, so he'll be running the climbing wall.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: Dina, you'll be on the zip wire. It's our most popular ride, and it needs someone calm and confident, which you clearly are.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: Ethan, you'll start in the café. It gets very busy at lunchtime, so be ready.

script.speaker: rachel
script.text: And Fiona, you'll be directing traffic in the car park in the mornings, and helping wherever you're needed in the afternoons. There's also a first-aid room, but only our qualified nurses work in there, so none of you will be based there.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 2. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

parts.title: A dissertation on remote working
parts.context: A student discusses her dissertation on working from home with her tutor.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Part 3. You will hear a business student, Hannah, talking to her tutor, Dr Patel, about her dissertation on remote working. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: Come in, Hannah. So, talk me through your research method from the beginning.

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: Well, first I read all the previous studies I could find on remote working, so that I knew what questions hadn't been answered yet.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: Good. And then?

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: Then I designed a questionnaire for employees, about their working hours, their productivity and how they felt about working from home.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: Did you test it before you sent it out?

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: Yes, I ran a pilot with a small group of ten people first, and I changed three questions that people found confusing.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: Very sensible. And the interviews?

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: After the questionnaire, I interviewed managers at three different companies, to get the employers' point of view.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: And how are you going to put your results in context?

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: I'm going to compare them with data from before the pandemic, when hardly anyone worked from home.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: I was worried that two hundred responses wasn't enough.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: For a dissertation at this level, two hundred is perfectly adequate. You don't need any more.

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: That's a relief. The results were interesting. I expected people to say they felt lonely, and some did. But what surprised me was that people working from home actually worked about an hour longer each day than in the office.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: That matches some recent research. Now, your literature review. At the moment you go through the studies one by one, in date order. It would be much stronger if you organised it by theme instead.

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: OK, I'll do that. To be honest, the part I'm finding hardest is the statistics. I'm fine with writing, but analysing the numbers takes me forever.

script.speaker: patel
script.text: The maths support centre runs drop-in sessions on Wednesdays. I'd go along. So, when can I see the next draft? By this Friday?

script.speaker: hannah
script.text: I've got two exams this week. Could I give it to you next Monday?

script.speaker: patel
script.text: Monday's fine.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 3. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

parts.title: Lecture: mangrove forests
parts.context: An environmental science lecture about mangrove forests and why they matter.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Part 4. You will hear a lecture about mangrove forests. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Good morning. Today's topic is one of the most unusual ecosystems on the planet: mangrove forests.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Mangroves are trees and shrubs that grow along tropical and subtropical coasts, in the zone between high and low tide. That means that twice a day their roots are under the sea, and twice a day they're out in the air.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Very few trees can live in salt water, but mangroves have found ways to cope. Many species filter the salt out through their roots, and others get rid of it through their leaves, where you can sometimes see tiny salt crystals.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Mud on the coast contains very little oxygen, so some mangroves grow special roots that point upwards, out of the mud, like snorkels. These roots take in oxygen from the air.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Their seeds are unusual too. They start to grow while they are still on the tree, so when they drop into the water, they are already young plants, ready to take root.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Why do mangroves matter? First, their thick roots slow down waves, so they protect the coast from storms and reduce erosion. Villages behind healthy mangroves have suffered far less damage from storms than villages without them.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Second, the calm water among the roots is a nursery for young fish, which later move out to the open sea. Many fishing communities depend on this.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: And third, mangroves store huge amounts of carbon, most of it in the mud beneath them, which helps to slow climate change.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Sadly, large areas of mangrove have been lost, and one of the biggest causes has been clearing them to make shrimp farms.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: The good news is that many communities are now restoring them by planting seedlings. But planting alone isn't enough. Projects only succeed when the seedlings are planted in places where the water can flow in and out naturally, with the tide. Where that has been blocked, the young trees simply die.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 4. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: That is the end of the Listening test.
